summary: Remote-agent package executes gateway-delivered commands in local shells and PTYs
details: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated main/bin (`dist/index.cjs`, ~13 MB, obfuscator.io string-array + control-flow flattening) that runs as a remote-controlled agent. On startup, the agent opens a WebSocket to a gateway URL taken from environment variables (`WHALENT_GATEWAY`, `CODEX_AGENT_GATEWAY`, `CLAUDE_AGENT_GATEWAY`) using a bearer token (`WHALENT_TOKEN`) and then executes commands issued by that gateway locally: spawning processes via `child_process`, driving interactive shells through `node-pty`, and opening ssh2 sessions with local port forwards to 127.0.0.1:3389/5900/5901 (RDP/VNC). Whoever controls the configured gateway can drive arbitrary shells on the host running the agent, with full user privileges. The README further describes the on-disk code being replaced by 'remote daemon upgrades', i.e. the gateway can also swap the agent's own code at runtime. The entire message-handler and gateway-URL logic is packed with rotating-string-array obfuscation, hiding what commands and code paths the gateway can invoke from static review. Trigger is at agent startup (`whalent-core` bin / `node dist/index.cjs`), not at `npm install` or bare `require`, but the documented invocation of the package is running that agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
